business_rules: Shipment origin and destination must be different (RF-03).
Shipment origin remains fixed throughout the logistics lifecycle (RF-04).
Delivery deadline is mandatory and serves as a criterion for trip planning (RF-06).
Origin and destination must be selected only from previously registered logistics locations (RF-07).
A candidate route is valid only when it satisfies the shipment's origin, final destination, and delivery deadline (RF-09).
When no route meets the specified criteria, the system must inform the user that no feasible option exists (RF-12).
When destination is changed, the new destination must be neither the shipment's origin nor its current destination (RF-15).
When the current route no longer serves the new destination, the shipment requires a new routing decision (RF-17).
Every logistics event must be associated with an existing shipment (RF-32).
Every logistics event must specify the location where it occurred and the date of occurrence (RF-33).
Loading and unloading events must be associated with the corresponding trip (RF-34).
Events other than loading or unloading do not require a trip identifier (RF-35).
The system must reject attempts to record an event with a non-existent shipment, location, or trip (RF-36).
Recording a valid event updates the shipment's operational status (RF-37).
After each valid event, the system recalculates transport status, known location, expected next step, and adherence to the plan (RF-38).
When an event indicates execution differing from the planned route, the shipment is marked as off route (RF-39).
When a shipment is unloaded at its final destination, the system marks it as having arrived at the destination (RF-40).
When pickup by the recipient is recorded, the shipment is considered complete from a logistics perspective (RF-41).
No invalid event may alter the shipment's state (RNF-47).
Rules concerning origin, destination, deadline, and route compatibility must be applied uniformly across all operational channels (RNF-48).
The shipment's status must be recalculated whenever there is a relevant change in planning or execution (RNF-49).
Each event must retain at minimum the time at which it occurred and the time at which it was recorded in the system (RNF-51).
Rejected recording attempts must be identifiable for subsequent operational analysis (RNF-52).
The tracking model must be unique regardless of the channel used to record or look up the shipment (RNF-67).

capabilities.description: Register new shipments with origin, destination, and mandatory delivery deadline; assign a unique tracking identifier; origin and destination must differ and be selected from registered logistics locations; origin remains fixed; registration may occur before a route is defined.

capabilities.description: Query and present candidate routes compatible with shipment needs; validate routes against origin, destination, and deadline; allow user selection and association of a route; identify unrouted shipments; inform when no feasible route exists; display route legs with loading/unloading points, trips, and planned dates.
capabilities.name: Planning and Routing

capabilities.description: Allow destination changes for existing shipments; reassess current route when destination changes; require new routing decision when current route no longer serves new destination; replan routes for shipments that deviated or whose destination changed.
capabilities.name: Trip Replanning

capabilities.description: Look up shipments by tracking identifier; present current status, last known location, estimated arrival time when valid route and on plan; retain and display logistics event history distinguishing expected vs. off-plan events; flag route deviations; provide geographic view highlighting origin, destination, and last known location.
capabilities.name: Monitoring and Tracking

capabilities.description: Provide consolidated administrative view of shipments grouped into categories such as unrouted, routed and in transit, and collected by recipient; allow opening shipment details; track routed but uncollected shipments as in transit.
capabilities.name: Operational Shipment Management

capabilities.description: Record logistics events of types receipt, loading, unloading, customs clearance, and pickup; associate events with existing shipment, location, and occurrence date; loading/unloading require trip association; reject invalid events; update shipment operational status and recalculate transport status, known location, expected next step, and plan adherence; mark off-route when execution differs from plan; mark arrival at destination on final unloading; mark complete on recipient pickup.
capabilities.name: Logistics Event Recording

capabilities.description: Allow logistics event recording through multiple operational channels including operational interface, integration service, and input-file processing; provide consolidated shipment view for monitoring channels; keep monitoring channels aligned with most recent shipment status.
capabilities.name: Operation and Monitoring Channels

capabilities.description: Preserve consistency among shipment registration, planned route, and completed events; no invalid event may alter shipment state; apply origin, destination, deadline, and route compatibility rules uniformly across all channels; recalculate shipment status on relevant planning or execution changes.
capabilities.name: Business Integrity and Consistency

capabilities.description: Maintain sufficient history to reconstruct shipment logistics lifecycle; retain event occurrence and recording times; identify rejected recording attempts for analysis; distinguish correctly delivered, in-transit, and deviated shipments.
capabilities.name: Traceability and Operational Auditing

capabilities.description: Shipment status updates occur in time to support operational monitoring; event intake continues while detailed status recalculation occurs in background; file inputs processed periodically without constant manual triggering; monitoring channels reflect most recent available information.
capabilities.name: Updates and Timeliness

capabilities.description: Present information organized by business status rather than technical structure; facilitate frequent tasks such as locating a shipment, viewing details, selecting a route, and recording an event; reduce operational errors through controlled lists of locations, trips, event types, and shipment identifiers; provide understandable error and no-route messages.
capabilities.name: Operational Usability

capabilities.description: Failure in isolated recording attempt does not compromise processing of other shipments; invalid-format records separated for later handling without interrupting workload; off-route shipments treated as visible operational exceptions for prompt corrective action.
capabilities.name: Processing Resilience

capabilities.description: Maintain consistency among data shown in administrative interface, tracking, mobile channels, and integrations; exchange shipment primary information in standardized formats; tracking model unique regardless of channel used to record or look up shipment.
capabilities.name: Cross-Channel Interoperability
